title: Cite it or it didn't happen
kicker: World 3 · Answer from the Source · Level 3

job.text: Same menu. New question: "Which drink is cheapest, and how much?" The answer must carry both the value and the menu row it came from, so a reader can verify it.

naivePrompt: Which drink is cheapest and how much?
basePrompt: Which drink is cheapest and how much?

text.plain: Answer in this format: drink, price, and which menu row it came from.
Fill all three fields from the same menu row — the price must belong to that drink.
text.tech: Bind all three fields to the one retrieved row object.

text.plain: Pick the row with the lowest price.
Quote the exact menu row text next to the answer.
text.tech: Return the raw matched row string alongside the fields.

rules.feedback: Checkable. The price belongs to the drink, it's the lowest on the menu, and you can see the exact row. Anyone can verify it in one glance.
rules.lesson: Cite the row and the answer verifies itself.

rules.claim: Cheapest: oat latte, $3.00, from menu row 1.
rules.feedback: Right shape, wrong wiring. The three fields came from different places, so the price still isn't the drink's. Fill them all from one row.
rules.lesson: A shape is only as good as where you fill it from.

rules.claim: The cheapest is the oat latte at $3.50.
rules.feedback: The price doesn't belong to that drink. It stitched a cheap price onto the wrong name — $3.50 is the drip coffee. 'Be confident' just made the mismatch sound sure.
rules.lesson: A confident pair can still be mismatched.

hints.nudge: Does the price actually belong to the drink it named?
hints.gap: The three fields came from different rows — that's how the price ended up on the wrong drink. Pin them to one row.
hints.moves: Add Name the shape, Fill it from one row, and Pick the lowest-price row.

whatYouDoDifferently.naive: "which is cheapest?" → a mismatched price and name.
whatYouDoDifferently.rewrite: "give drink, price and the row, all from one row, lowest price" → a cited, verifiable answer.

template.plain: Give me the answer and the exact line in the document it came from, together. The value and its source must be from the same place.
template.tech: Return {answer, source_row} where both fields are bound to the same retrieved row; the value must come from the cited row.

notes: ChatGPT: ask for a tiny table: answer | source line. If it can't fill the source, don't trust the answer.
Copilot in Excel: have the lookup return the row number too, so the source is visible.
A chat AI that can't run code: make it quote the source line next to the answer; a quote you can check beats a number you can't. Never accept 'I checked, it's right'.
